title: United Express 5925
summary: United Express Flight 5925 descended for landing at Quincy, a non-towered airport, on runway 13. A Beechcraft King Air began takeoff on intersecting runway 4 without proper monitoring of radio traffic. A GPWS sound in the United Express cockpit prevented the crew from receiving a complete transmission about aircraft holding positions. Both aircraft collided at the runway intersection and caught fire. All 14 occupants died from smoke inhalation.
probable_cause: King Air pilots' failure to effectively monitor the common traffic advisory frequency and scan for traffic. Contributing factor: simultaneous transmission by Cherokee aircraft that blocked the United Express crew's awareness.

factors.evidence: King Air pilots failed to effectively monitor both the common frequency and to scan for traffic
GPWS sound prevented clear reception of transmission regarding aircraft positions and holding status
King Air occupied Runway 4 during United Express landing on intersecting Runway 13 without proper coordination
Both aircraft destroyed by fire; all survivors trapped inside by jammed door and died from smoke inhalation

events.text: Flight 5925 departed Chicago O'Hare with 10 passengers plus crew
Aircraft made intermediate stop at Burlington, Iowa
Captain Gathje inquired whether King Air would hold short or depart before Flight 5925 arrival
Ground proximity warning system emitted sound in cockpit during critical transmission
Flight 5925 landed on Runway 13 believing both aircraft were holding short
King Air taxied into position on Runway 4 and had begun its takeoff roll when Flight 5925 landed
Aircraft collided at intersection of runways, skidded 110 feet and caught fire
